thread:
tim: FYI customer 'Sawtooth' wants BYO keys for the POC. They want an on-prem HSM-backed key ceremony and automated 30-day rotation. Asking if we can support offline key ceremony + our SOW delta and pricing impact.

akash: Do we have a recommended runbook for BYO-HSM POC? They asked about network egress and latency impact too.

jen: Short answer: yes, we support BYO keys via our Key Proxy flow and CloudHSM/Thales integrations. Differences: (1) onboarding runbook + attestation step, (2) additional ops time for key ceremony, (3) potential uplift for HSM transport & escrow.

jen: Also, rotation every 30d is fine but depends on customer workload. If they want zero-downtime rotation we need to enable dual-key serving during rollout which adds ~10-20% ops complexity.

leo-cust: Confirming: we need dual-key during rotation so we can failback quickly. Also need a pre-signed key escrow option in case of emergency. Is that in your standard POC?

jen: We can include pre-signed escrow as an add-on in the POC SOW. Standard POC includes key import, KMS integration, and one rotation test. Escrow and repeated ceremonies are billable.

akash: Can you paste a minimal example of the config we'd expect them to run on their side? I want to prep docs for their infra team.

jen: Sure — short snippet they can run during POC (they'll replace placeholders):

```yaml
# redwood keyproxy sample
key_management:
  mode: BYO
  hsm: {
    vendor: "thales",
    endpoint: "hsm.internal:1800",
    attestation_cert: "/tmp/attest.crt"
  }
  rotation:
    strategy: dual-key
    window_days: 2
    frequency_days: 30
```

jen: Note: they must open port 1800 (or equivalent) to our key proxy endpoint. We provide a NATed relay for air-gapped setups but that's an extra ops step.

tim: Pricing note — BYO-HSM add-on is typically +25-35% on top of POC engineering hours depending on travel/attestation and escrow handling. If they accept remote attestation only (no physical transport) we can drop to +15%.

sales-ops: Echoing — for SOW we need: scope (1 import ceremony, 1 rotation test), hours estimate (16-40h depending on escrow), and a rate-card line for "Key Escrow / Physical HSM ops". Will draft.

leo-cust: They also flagged regulatory requirement: keys must never leave their control plane and audit logs must be shipped to their SIEM. Can we stream audit logs to their collector?

jen: Yes — we support streaming audit events to customer SIEM via syslog/forwarder. That will be in the SOW as a configuration task and needs their collector endpoint details.

security-bot: Automated note: data handling checklist required — attestation artifacts, rotation proof (signatures), and key lineage must be recorded.

akash: Two quick blockers for internal: (1) confirm if we can do pre-signed escrow under our current legal terms (legal ok?), (2) check latency/regression risk when dual-keying for serving — does this increase p99 by more than ~10ms?

jen: On (1) I'll sync with legal, but historically pre-signed escrow is allowed with cust-signed SLA and approved retention policy. On (2) engineering: dual-key serving adds an extra KMS lookup on first token of a session; typical p99 delta is 5-12ms on our infra depending on region. We should run a perf check in staging.

tim: Action items: jen to send POC SOW draft + attestation checklist by EOD tomorrow; sales-ops to add pricing lines and range; akash to schedule a short perf run with eng-runtime for p99 impact. leo-cust to confirm SIEM endpoint and whether physical key courier is required.

leo-cust: Thanks — will get SIEM details and confirm courier requirement by Friday.

tim: :thumbsup: If legal has an issue we can offer escrow via a 3rd-party custodian as fallback (higher cost).

jen: I'll also include a short runbook section in the SOW about rollbacks and emergency key revocation steps.

sales-ops: Drafting SOW now, will drop version in this thread when ready for review.

akash: Great — ping me once SOW is in thread, I'll loop eng-runtime and infra.

tim: Thanks everyone. Short and focused thread — appreciate the quick turnaround.
